title: Volume 1 Chapter 4 — Experimental Unit
content: A few days had passed since the ambush.
Since it was Sunday, the Academy was on holiday, and I had been on standby since morning in the hangar loaned to the Prometheus Project development team.
"All right, all right!"
"Hury up and remove the fixtures!"
"Make sure to double-check the contents of the containers!"
The mechanics were busily moving around since morning.
In the hangar, which had completed preparations for acceptance, the delivery of the experimental unit—the core of the project—was underway.
Watching the experimental unit from a corner to stay out of the way, I mumbled my impressions as its tarps were stripped away, leaving it standing inside the hangar.
"This is the first time I've ever seen a real humanoid weapon."
Humanoid weapons, once highly anticipated and developed for anti-Gijuu use, proved useless on the battlefield, leading to the cancellation of the development project itself.
The development team had salvaged the stored unit, performed maintenance and modifications, and transported it to the Third Academy.
Dr. Allison was standing beside me as well.
While occasionally glancing at the busily moving mechanics, she had brought out a folding chair and sat down.
She was operating a tablet terminal, checking the upcoming schedule.
Dr. Allison's gaze remained fixed on the tablet screen.

"It's been over ten years since the project was canceled, hasn't it? The experimental unit we brought seems to be a machine that was sleeping in some warehouse. Apparently, the maintenance was quite an ordeal."
"Does a machine from over ten years ago actually run?"

"We made it run. In the first place, the Prometheus Project doesn't have any major track record. There are limits to the budget the organization provides for us. We have to use whatever is available."
"Is this what they call 'a harsh world'?"

From my perspective, we should utilize whatever we can, but the lack of leeway to develop a brand-new machine for the project felt like a telling reflection of the development team's current situation.
"I didn't expect you to use a phrase like 'harsh world.'"
As Dr. Allison looked up with genuine curiosity, I found myself remembering a man who used to complain a lot.
"A foul-mouthed comrade of mine used to say it often."
"Oh, is that so?"
Losing interest in my explanation, Dr. Allison turned her gaze back toward the experimental unit.
Freed from its fixtures, the heavily armored experimental unit looked incredibly heavy just from its appearance.
As I gazed at it, an oddly high-spirited, mushroom-haired doctor entered the hangar.
It was Dr. Smith.

"Hifumi-kun, have you been well? I was surprised when I heard you were transferred into Class 5, but seeing you here now, it looks like you're managing well enough. Even so, the Principal of the Third Academy truly amazes me with her way of thinking. I fully expected her to keep her distance, so I never imagined she would actually have you mingle with the Valkyries. The Principal who accepted our development team is definitely an eccentric, isn't she?"
Finishing everything he wanted to say along with his greeting, Dr. Smith approached Dr. Allison before even waiting for my reply, looking thoroughly satisfied.
"Allison-kun, I'm glad to see you're doing well too. More importantly, will you listen to this? During the maintenance of the experimental unit, a new idea—"
He tried to rattle on to Dr. Allison this time, but the two of them seemed to have a long history together.
Showing no intention of listening to a long-winded speech, she cut him off with a swift reply.
"Yes, I'm fine. Also, let's leave the talk about the experimental unit for later. Now that we have both the pilot and the machine together, I want to finalize our upcoming schedule."
She certainly seemed to know exactly how to handle Dr. Smith.
Though his speech was cut short, Dr. Smith didn't seem to mind in the slightest.
"True. For now, shall we begin with the activation experiment of the experimental unit?"
Hearing about the activation experiment for a humanoid weapon, I asked about a point of doubt.
"Dr. Smith, may I ask a question?"
"What is it, Hifumi-kun?"
"I heard that the experimental unit underwent maintenance on the ground. Couldn't the activation experiment have been performed on the ground as well?"

"Ah, of course. It moved without any issues on the ground. However, that was strictly when operated by a conventional pilot. If you board a machine outfitted with a magic converter, we cannot guarantee that anomalies won't occur. After all, experiments involving magic must be done at the Academy. Look, it's a massive cluster of classified tech, anyway."
Since the installed equipment might cause issues, an experiment was indeed necessary.
Dr. Allison also appeared to favor the activation experiment.
"You were originally an infantryman, not a pilot, after all. We plan to conduct actual machine training in parallel with the activation experiments."
"Thank you very much for answering my questions."
When I offered a formal salute, Dr. Smith burst into laughter.
"Hifumi-kun, you're the same as always. With that attitude, aren't you going to stick out at this academy?"
"Yes, I am fully aware that I stand out."
Just having a guy inside a classroom at an all-girls school made me stand out, but apparently, my personality was also vastly detached from that of a conventional male student.
I had at least that much awareness of my isolation within Class 5.
Dr. Allison let out a deep sigh at my reply.
"What a spirited response."
"Thank you very much."
"It was sarcasm. You ought to study common sense along with Dr. Smith."
Told by Dr. Allison to learn common sense, Dr. Smith, who had assumed himself unrelated until midway through, looked startled to hear his name mentioned.
"Eh, me too?"
Changing into my pilot suit, I slid my body into the cramped cockpit of the experimental unit.
It seemed it was originally narrow enough to make even moving around an ordeal, but with the addition of experimental instruments, it had become even more claustrophobic.
Sitting in the pilot's seat and fastening my seatbelt, I dispassionately entered preparations to boot up the machine.
"Test pilot Warrant Officer Hifumi Ren, commencing activation of the prototype experimental unit XFA-10 Thunderbolt Modified Model."
As I relayed this to the development team over the intercom, Dr. Smith's face was projected onto the activated monitor.
There didn't seem to be any particular issues, but it appeared he had a personal point of curiosity.
『Hmm, too stiff. Let's take it a bit more easy, Hifumi-kun.』
"Easy, you say? Even if you tell me that, I simply—"
At my reply, which was often criticized for lacking a sense of humor, Dr. Smith held up his palm toward me.
Understanding it as a gesture to close my mouth, I fell silent.
After pondering for a short moment, Dr. Smith nodded several times with a smile.

『The machine's name can just be Thunderbolt. Even if we call it a modified model, it's an experimental unit that was never officially adopted, after all. The real issue is your callsign, Hifumi-kun. In times like these, shouldn't a pilot be addressed by a callsign?』
"A callsign? ...Back when I belonged to the infantry unit, I was called Cherry."
Uttering that nostalgic callsign caused a tight, squeezing sensation in my chest for some reason.
On the other side of the monitor, Dr. Smith tilted his head.
『Hifumi-kun is Cherry? A cherry is a callsign that doesn't connect with your image at all. Is there some kind of meaning behind it?』
"That is because I—"
As I attempted to explain the meaning, Dr. Allison interrupted the conversation with a deliberately loud clearing of her throat.
『Let's change the callsign to something new. Do you have any preferences, Warrant Officer?』
"No, I have an attachment to Cherry."
『...Dr. Smith, do you have any preferences?』
Evidently, it wasn't the response Dr. Allison wanted, as she turned to ask Dr. Smith for his opinion on the callsign.
『Aiphazpht... that might be a bit difficult to pronounce. In that case, let's go with Envy. Yes, starting today, Hifumi-kun's callsign is Envy.』
Beside a thoroughly satisfied Dr. Smith, Dr. Allison's exasperated face was projected.
『For you, Dr. Smith, that carries quite a bit of sarcasm. Is that a criticism of the higher-ups?』
Criticism of the higher-ups sounded highly unsettling, so I couldn't remain silent either.
"I believe critical speech and conduct are ill-advised, sir?"
To my concerned remark, Dr. Smith smiled while adjusting his glasses with his middle finger.
『"Aiphazpht" translates to jealousy in Japanese. The same goes for Envy. Furthermore, it's a fitting callsign derived from us, who are envious of the Valkyries' power. Don't you think so?』
"Envy, you say..."
While I questioned the propriety of having 'Envy' as a callsign, memories of being given the callsign 'Cherry' by my previous platoon resurfaced.
Apparently, in old-era militaries, they would deliberately assign strange callsigns.
Following the Gijuu invasion, it was the Fairy Agency that reorganized the collapsed military forces.
Even after the reorganization, the traditions of the military remained, handed down to the present day.
To go from being called Cherry to being called Envy... should I say it felt strangely familiar? It reminded me of my old platoon, so I didn't dislike it.
Furthermore, if I switched from Cherry to Envy, my former platoon comrades probably would have teased me for being 'way too cool.'
"...I agree. Callsign Envy, acknowledged."
When I concurred with Dr. Smith's opinion, Dr. Allison knit her brows.
『I didn't expect you to agree as well. ...I'm really registering you as Envy. Don't blame me if you complain about it later.』
『It'll be fine. In fact, the Valkyries of Japan might even be pleased, don't you think? We're merely renting space here, after all. Let's display a humble attitude toward them.』
Addressing ourselves as Envy to curry favor with the female students of the Third Academy. It sounded like a poignant summary of our development team's current standing.
The activation of the Thunderbolt proceeded without a hitch.
The activation tests had fundamentally been completed before transport, and the machine had been brought in under the evaluation that it operated normally.
Steering the booted-up Thunderbolt from the cockpit, I was currently conducting walking trials in a courtyard prepared near the hangar.
Though designated a courtyard, it was stacked with shipping containers, leaving only a highly restricted amount of usable space.
When the development team pleaded for a testing ground, the academy administration had apparently assigned them this thoroughly unorganized sector.
If you want to secure a testing space, clean it up yourselves—that was the implication.
Presently, treating the containers slated for clearance as obstacles, the Thunderbolt walked along the designated course toward the finish line.
"I have arrived at the destination."
As I successfully guided the machine to the finish line without issue, the development team offered a light round of applause.
Alongside the applause filtering through the comms, Dr. Allison's voice chimed in.
『Everything seems fine. I want to clear the vast majority of our checklist items by the end of today, so remain on standby inside the cockpit until preparations for the next test are complete.』
"Its contents are acknowledged."
Ordered to wait inside the cramped cockpit, I reviewed the controls to familiarize myself with the operation as quickly as possible.
"The control stick is stiffer than the simulator's. The pedals could afford to be a bit heavier."
Compiling the necessary feedback for the next round of adjustments upon my return, I magnified the monitor display.
Switching through thermography and various sensor feeds, I attempted to hardwire the data into my physical memory.
As I verified each parameter individually, the sheer exorbitant cost of a humanoid weapon truly sank in.
"It's completely night and day compared to the suits we used back in the infantry. If we had this level of performance..."
Would the mortality rate in ground combat have drastically dropped? Pondering that far, I ultimately realized the insurmountable bottleneck of cost-effectiveness and shook my head.
"...There is no point in dwelling on it now, I suppose. Even so, despite possessing this much armor, it has no practical effect against Class 2 Gijuu or higher."
Apparently, when humanoid weapons were first conceived, almost every unit was a heavy-armor type.
The reasoning stemmed from the conclusion that thick armor plating was an absolute necessity to withstand attacks from Class 2 Gijuu and above.
However, such dense armor plating had supposedly proven entirely meaningless before the monsters.
An armor plating devoid of a forcefield—devoid of magic—merely solidified the established dogma that conventional defenses were useless in combat against the Gijuu.
Furthermore, unless a forcefield could be channeled into offensive maneuvers, one could not inflict effective damage upon the Gijuu.
Humanoid weapons had ultimately concluded as nothing more than providing the enemy with an oversized target.
"...If it is a machine outfitted with a magic converter, this dilemma can be resolved."
The Prometheus Project sought to install a magic converter into a humanoid weapon system that had previously been written off as a mere target.
The justification for mounting it on a humanoid frame was that the magic converter itself was far too massive for ground infantry to carry.

There had apparently been proposals to mount it on tanks or fighter jets, but the decision ultimately settled on repurposing the humanoid weapons, which had absorbed astronomical budgets only to end in failure.

According to Dr. Smith, 'a humanoid form is more efficient,' but the precise logistics surrounding that claim involved deep security classifications and had not been disclosed to a mere test pilot like me.
Nevertheless, there was no doubt that utilizing a humanoid weapon held definitive significance.
"Hm?"
Pivoting the unit's camera eye, I noticed a group of female students observing us from a distance.
There were roughly six of them in total, but among them was a highly distinct student.
The manner in which the other students deferred to her was palpable even through the monitor feed.
The girl whose red hair fluttered in the breeze wore a highly characteristic cape.
"A crimson cape... Is that Hayase-san?"
Since I had never seen any other student at the academy wearing a crimson cape, there was no mistaking her identity.
As I muttered to myself inside the cockpit, Hayase-san knit her brows in apparent displeasure, as if sensing my gaze, and turned on her heel to leave.
It appeared she exchanged a word or two with the surrounding students.
Following closely behind Hayase-san, the other girls departed as well.
"She noticed my gaze from this distance? ...Surely not."
Perhaps intrigued by my audible mumbling, Dr. Smith spoke to me over the channel.
『Talking to yourself?』
"Apologies, sir. I detected several female students from the academy observing our experiment."
『Ah, that's not ideal. This is technically a top-secret experiment, so it's problematic if we're being watched.』
"Should we notify the academy administration?"
『Well, given that we are merely renting space here, the administration would likely shield the students anyway. Out of curiosity, what kind of girls were watching?』
"The most distinct among them was Hayase-san... the student wearing the crimson cape."
As I relayed Hayase-san's identifying traits, Dr. Allison cut into the conversation.
『That would be the Ace. Even if we lodged a formal complaint with the academy, she wouldn't face any substantial reprimand.』
"The Ace?"

『There are four colors of capes—blue, green, yellow... and red. Permission to wear one is strictly reserved for the definitive Ace of each class. Since the Aces are critical combat assets for the academy, a verbal warning would be the absolute extent of it.』
"Hayase-san is the academy's Ace... No, that aligns perfectly."
She possessed immense capability and radiated absolute confidence.
Louise had also evaluated her combat strength exceptionally highly, so there was no doubt about it.
However, much like the other students, she wore a severe expression, suggesting she opposed the Prometheus Project.
The gaze she leveled at the Thunderbolt was saturated with naked revulsion.
The following day.
During a break in the Class 5 classroom, I was speaking with Louise.
Our topic was the events of yesterday.
"Hayase-san—Hayase Maya—is undeniably the Ace of Boots Cat."
Confused by the unfamiliar terminology, I echoed her words.
"Boots Cat? Is that her callsign?"
Shaking her head, Louise thoroughly explained the inner workings of the academy to me.
"Classes 1 through 4 each have a specific color and designation. For instance, Class 1's color is blue and their name is Bluebird. In the case of Class 3, the color is red and the name is Boots Cat."
"Like a squadron name, then?"
Placing a hand to my chin, I processed it in my own way, and Louise nodded to confirm I wasn't mistaken.

"Exactly. They act as class designations normally, but on the battlefield, they function as squadron names. Furthermore, permission to wear the crimson cape is granted exclusively to Hayase-san. So if there was a girl wearing a crimson cape there, it was definitely her."

"I have heard that a colored cape is proof of an Ace. ...However, why would someone of her standing be in that sector? I find it difficult to believe an Ace would flagrantly disregard the directives of the Base Commander."
"I suppose I don't know the answer to that either."
Dr. Allison had mentioned that the academy administration issued explicit notices to stay away due to the highly classified nature of the Prometheus Project.
As the academy's Ace, did she occupy a role akin to a representative for the entire student body?
The discipline and protocols here were far too detached from a standard military outpost, forcing me to speculate, but she undeniably occupied an exceptionally high-profile position.
Hayase Maya... I preferred not to believe that the Ace was the type of person who would simply ignore standing orders.
As I pondered, three female students approached us.
Judging by their expressions, an atmosphere that could hardly be considered amicable radiated from them.
Completely ignoring Louise, they addressed me directly.
Slamming a hand onto my desk, they adopted an overtly threatening stance toward me.
"Hey, is it true you regenerated your lost limbs using Gijuu cells?"
Had I let my guard down for a single second, I likely would have reacted in visible agitation to her words.
Killing my emotions, I maintained a strict poker face.
The singular thought that flashed through my mind was: *How did they find out?*
The regenerative surgery utilizing Gijuu cells was strictly classified under the protocols of the Prometheus Project.
It wasn't the type of information that could be deduced simply by observing the Thunderbolt.
Suddenly, the assailants who identified themselves as 'Fallen Angels' came to mind.
Where did the leak originate? Did those attackers spread the information? The imperative to notify the doctors immediately raced through my mind.
"...I do not comprehend the intent of your question."
I attempted to deflect the matter and contact the research team, but the confrontational student refused to let me slip away.
Before I knew it, the word *Gijuu* caught the attention of the surrounding students, plunging the previously boisterous classroom into dead silence.
The entire room directed piercing, hostile glares toward me.
"Don't play dumb. The information is already circulating. You regenerated the limbs you lost on the battlefield using Gijuu cells, didn't you?"
How far had the leak spread? While feeling a surge of urgency, I feigned absolute composure and calculated a method to defuse the situation.
Glancing at the classroom clock, I noted that the instructor would arrive in just a few minutes.
I could wait, but this constituted a genuine emergency.
It would be wiser to bypass the lecture entirely, regroup with the development team, and deliberate on our next steps.
As I prepared to stand up, I realized the other female students had already moved to cut off my paths of retreat.
Several girls blocked the classroom exit, while the remainder advanced to surround my desk.
Naked hostility resided in every pair of eyes.
The student who had interrogated me wore a severe, unyielding expression.
"I kept wondering how a guy who can't even manipulate magic was supposed to fight the Gijuu. I never imagined you'd use Gijuu cells to graft your limbs back on, though."
To these students who underwent grueling training specifically to eradicate the Gijuu, I was apparently viewed as little different from the monsters themselves.
The topic shifted to include the ambush from a few days prior.
"Is it true you wielded the power of a Gijuu when you were attacked?"
Nearly letting a gasp slip out, I tightly clenched both hands to endure the shock.
I hadn't anticipated that intelligence as recent as the prior incident would already be compromised.
"Don't just stand there silent, say something. Or would you prefer to be taken down right here?"
Whether they had secured them beforehand, several students had knives concealed beneath their cardigans.
As I evaluated a method to forcefully break through, Louise spread her arms defensively and stepped between me and the hostile students.
"Everyone, that's enough! The teacher is going to arrive any second!"
Right as Louise raised her voice, the instructor appeared at the classroom threshold.
Sensing the volatile atmosphere in the room, he crossed his arms and observed the scene.
Letting the situation progress, he made no immediate move to intervene.
"If you will excuse me."
I stood up intending to retreat to the development hangar, but Louise firmly gripped my arm and refused to let go.
"No. You need to stay in the classroom, Ren-kun."
As Louise issued her plea, one of the silent students barked out furiously.
"Louise, that guy is the enemy! Do you have any idea how many of our seniors and comrades his kind has slaughtered? If you're going to shield him, we won't show you any mercy either!"
Watching the girls reach for their weapons, I prepared to step forward to shield Louise.
Yet, Louise spoke up before I could move.

"Ren-kun is here precisely because the Principal and the administration authorized it. Everyone, let's calm down for a moment. Do you truly believe the leadership remains ignorant of his circumstances?"
Louise's flawless logic evidently held weight with the confrontational students.
"Tch! You absolute softie!"
Releasing their grips on their weapons, the girls relented under Louise's persuasion and returned to their desks.
As the remaining students dispersed, the instructor finally stepped into the room.
"You all were remarkably boisterous. Honestly, the Principal's whims are quite a headache. Let me make this clear as a precaution: do not incite disturbances."
Though his stance had been passive, the instructor shot a stern look at the students who had smuggled weapons into the classroom.

"If you cause a scene, it wouldn't be surprising if your scout offers or recommendations vanish entirely. If you wish to avoid graduating as a permanent member of Class 5, you had best exercise self-restraint."
At his warning, an instantaneous wave of palpable tension rippled through every single student.
They reacted with extreme sensitivity to the concepts of scouts, recommendations... and graduation.
As I quietly attempted to depart the room, Louise gestured for me to remain seated.
"I have something to tell you later, so stay here for now."
"However, I am under an official obligation to notify the development team of this operational breakdown."
"What if... I told you I have an idea of who leaked the information?"
Hearing Louise claim she possessed a lead regarding the source of the leak, I was undeniably caught off guard.
"You know who it is?"
Louise gave a subtle, solemn nod.
"Our next break is lunch hour. Let's speak then."
"...With its context acknowledged."
Desperate for any lead, I fired off a quick message to Dr. Allison to alert her to the security compromise before focus-shifting back to the lectures.
Once the lunch bell rang, Louise escorted me up to the school building's rooftop.
"Is this sector not strictly off-limits? There was an explicit warning sign posted along the staircase."
Standing near the perimeter fencing, Louise detailed her reasoning for selecting this location.
"Sorry about that. But nobody will come up here."
"You require absolute privacy, then."
Based on her evasive behavior, providing me with this intelligence evidently carried severe disadvantages for her as well.
The data she was risking exposure to share with me was not definitive proof.
There was no hard evidence. However, she appeared entirely convinced of her deduction.
"I don't have absolute confirmation either, but hearing your account brought a singular possibility to mind."
"A clue from my account?"
"It's Hayase-san."
As I murmured in surprise, Louise laid out her logic with methodical precision.
"Think about it, Hayase-san was present when you activated your capabilities during the ambush. She undoubtedly overheard your exchange with the assailants as well."
True, Hayase-san possessed direct knowledge regarding my condition, making her a highly plausible candidate for the source.
"No, I had operating under the assumption that the attackers themselves were leaking it... especially since Dr. Allison suspected an inside job."
Louise promptly refuted my line of reasoning.
"Doing that would be equivalent to broadcasting their own complicity, wouldn't it? If the origin of the intelligence were scrutinized, they would be the ones backed into a corner."
Acknowledging the validity of her perspective, I pivoted to query a detail that had lingered in my mind since the ambush.
"Come to think of it, who exactly were those assailants? Do you happen to know something about them, Louise?"
"Eh? W-What makes you think that?"
For a fleeting micro-second, Louise's eyes darted away.
"I am not suggesting you are affiliated with the attackers. However, given that you exchanged words in a foreign tongue, I surmised you might possess some insight."
What exactly had been communicated between Louise and the leader during that brief window?
Confronted with my question, Louise offered a somewhat strained smile.
"When I get frantic, the language of my homeland tends to slip out automatically... I wasn't doing it intentionally."
Recalling our past interactions, I remembered that Louise did occasionally utter French phrases.
"Right, of course."
Satisfied with her explanation, Louise detailed the context of that moment.
"I was startled too. I didn't expect them to casually respond to a phrase I uttered completely on instinct."
"What did you say to each other?"
"It happened so fast I can't recall the specifics, but it felt like she was mocking me."
"...Is an external foreign faction orchestrating this?"

"Who can say? Her Japanese was entirely fluent, after all. Besides, plenty of students here are capable of speaking multiple languages. There are many girls whose homelands are overseas like me, and study abroad programs have been on the rise."
While external infiltration was deemed mathematically improbable, it couldn't be entirely ruled out.
The identity of the culprit became even more obscured.
Louise, seemingly entirely convinced of Hayase-san's guilt, pressed her point with absolute certainty.

"To return to our main point, you mentioned she was observing your trial yesterday alongside a group of students, right? I suspect Hayase-san utilized her special privileges as an Ace to access those classified files."
"Why would an Ace possess that level of administrative privilege?"
From my military background, such a protocol was entirely incomprehensible.
While Aces were heavily prioritized in an army, that status did not automatically grant authorization to view top-secret intelligence.
Without the corresponding rank or specific posting, accessing classified data remained strictly forbidden.
Averting her eyes slightly from mine, Louise addressed my confusion.

"It's because the academy is a military apparatus, yet at the same time, it isn't a true military. I've been told the Aces are granted immense latitude, and I believe accessing classified intelligence falls within their clearance."
She meant that while it was an institution modeled after a military force, it lacked the rigid legal boundaries of a real army.
I had encountered nothing but structural shocks since my arrival, yet the notion that an Ace wielded clearance entirely disproportionate to her station was baffling.
An Ace, magnificent as she might be, was ultimately just a singular combat asset.
She was fundamentally not in a position where she should be permitted casual access to classified tech.
While I sat thoroughly speechless, Louise continued her breakdown, weaving in her own deductions regarding the classroom confrontation.
"She likely leaked your data to the Class 5 girls. I've heard Hayase-san harbors a deep, personal grudge against the Gijuu, so I imagine she finds the experiment you underwent entirely unforgivable."
"A personal grudge?"
"Yes. A massive gate outbreak occurred ten years ago, didn't it? It seems she went through a great deal during that disaster."
Countless individuals harbored a burning hatred for the Gijuu.
Particularly given the scale of the catastrophe ten years ago, it was entirely logical for someone of Hayase-san's generation to carry profound personal trauma.
Louise cast her gaze downward, staring at the floor.
"I was told she wasn't directly in the blast radius, but she suffered terribly under the collateral fallout."
The world had been in absolute chaos back then.
I, too, had lost my entire family during that exact same large-scale outbreak.
From that point onward, I was dispatched to the agency's facility and molded into a weapon.
"I can entirely comprehend why Hayase-san would despise my existence."
"Ren-kun?"
Louise looked mildly taken aback by how readily I accepted Hayase-san's hostile motivations.
However, even if I understood her perspective, halting the testing phase was a statistical impossibility.
"As it stands, this project constitutes my entire reason for existing right now. Even if I sympathize with her view, I cannot abort the trials without an official command."
As it stood, I was merely the test pilot of a prototype weapon system—a test subject grafted with Gijuu tissue.
For someone created solely for the sake of the Prometheus Project, ensuring the success of these trials was the singular directive left to me.
Louise locked her gaze onto mine.
"Are you certain you're fine with that? I suspect Hayase-san and her faction will try to sabotage your efforts going forward."
To a deeply concerned Louise, I offered an observation from my own history.
"I regularly weathered malicious harassment during my time in the ground forces. I am fully capable of handling it."
At my definitive declaration, a soft smile played on Louise's lips.
Clasping her hands behind her back, she leaned slightly forward, peering up at me through her eyelashes.
"You're incredibly reliable, Ren-kun. In that case, I'll lend you my strength. Please consult with me if anything happens, okay?"
"You have my gratitude."
When I offered an automatic salute, Louise initially looked stunned before bursting into a soft chuckle.
"Oh, honestly, I told you that you don't need to salute at times like this."
"My apologies. The conditioning is exceptionally difficult to shake off."
As I stood there perplexed by my own hardwired reflexes, Louise pressed her hands together.
"Wait, did you just smile? You smiled, didn't you?"
"Did I? I hold no personal awareness of it."
Had my expression truly shifted into a smile just now?
"You definitely did. You gave a small, sheepish smile, so there's no mistaking it. Yup, seeing you gradually adapt since coming to the academy gives me a real sense of relief, Ren-kun."
Despite being chronologically younger than me, Louise consistently adopted a maternal or elder-sisterly dynamic.
Undeniably, to someone evaluating me through the lens of baseline societal knowledge, I likely appeared remarkably helpless.
"If you ever hit a true wall, please let me know. I promise I will save you."
"Thank you very much."
I never could have anticipated receiving words of that nature from a younger girl.
Regardless, drawing the direct ire of the academy's premier Ace was a severe operational bottleneck.
If Louise's analytical assessment held true, Hayase-san wielded an administrative clearance that would be utterly impossible within a standard military hierarchy.
Navigating this obstacle from my current rank would undeniably introduce highly volatile complications.
"Now, if you will excuse me, I must regroup with the development team to brief them on these developments."
As I exited the rooftop, Louise offered a parting wave.
"Make sure you're back in time for the afternoon classes!"
